title: How do we share one thousand three hundred and twenty four into four?
description: One Thousand, three Hundreds, two Tens and four Ones are shared into four equal groups. A Thousand that cannot be shared is regrouped into ten Hundreds, and a leftover Hundred into ten Tens. Keeko's doubt is that the Thousand can be left out.
teaching_notes: One idea: when a place cannot be shared, regroup it into ten of the next smaller place and join it to the blocks already there. Watch for students who drop the block they cannot share.

video_script.why: The child can share small numbers but has not regrouped a leftover into the next place.
video_script.substitution: A Thousand that cannot be shared becomes ten Hundreds, and a leftover Hundred becomes ten Tens.
video_script.anchor: One thousand three hundred and twenty four, shared into four equal groups
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko leaves out the Thousand because it cannot be shared into four, and shares only three hundred and twenty four.
video_script.payoff_line: One thousand three hundred and twenty four divided by four is three hundred and thirty one.
maths_rules: the slip: 324 / 4 = 81, and 81 x 4 = 324, one Thousand short of 1324
video_script.design: The place-value blocks stay on the board; each regrouping breaks one block into ten of the next smaller place.
open_questions: The old doubt in the migration note (three Thousands, three Hundreds, three Tens and one One) did not hold together, so Keeko's doubt is that the Thousand is left out.

beats.on_screen: title card From your book; place-value blocks: 1 Thousand, 3 Hundreds, 2 Tens, 4 Ones above four empty groups

marks.num: the blocks appear above four empty groups
marks.ask: a question mark glows over one group

narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is an example from your book about sharing with place value.
<bookmark mark='num'/>The number is one thousand three hundred and twenty four. It is shared into four equal groups.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>How much does each group get?

beats.on_screen: the blocks and the four groups stay on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: Th H T O columns; one Thousand block breaking into ten Hundred blocks

marks.blocks: the blocks sit in columns Thousands, Hundreds, Tens and Ones
marks.break: one block breaks into ten blocks of the next smaller place
marks.name: the word regrouping is written

narration: <bookmark mark='blocks'/>Look at the blocks, one Thousand, three Hundreds, two Tens and four Ones.
<bookmark mark='break'/>One block can break into ten blocks of the next smaller place.
<bookmark mark='name'/>Breaking one block into ten smaller blocks is called regrouping.

beats.on_screen: Given: 1 Thousand + 3 Hundreds + 2 Tens + 4 Ones, shared into 4 equal groups

marks.given: the blocks and the four groups are written

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, one Thousand, three Hundreds, two Tens and four Ones, to be shared into four equal groups.

beats.on_screen: To find: what each of the 4 groups gets

marks.find: the share of one group is outlined

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find how much each of the four groups gets.

beats.on_screen: 1 Thousand cannot be shared into 4; regroup: 1 Thousand = 10 Hundreds; 10 + 3 = 13 Hundreds; 13 Hundreds ÷ 4: 3 Hundreds each, 1 Hundred remains

marks.s1a: the Thousand is tried and cannot be shared
marks.s1b: it breaks into ten Hundreds, which join the three Hundreds
marks.s1c: three Hundreds go to each group and one Hundred remains

narration: <bookmark mark='s1a'/>Step one, share the Thousand. One Thousand cannot be shared into four groups as it is.
<bookmark mark='s1b'/>Regroup it into ten Hundreds. Ten Hundreds and three Hundreds make thirteen Hundreds.
<bookmark mark='s1c'/>Thirteen Hundreds divided by four gives each group three Hundreds, and one Hundred remains.

beats.on_screen: 1 Hundred = 10 Tens; 10 + 2 = 12 Tens; 12 Tens ÷ 4 = 3 Tens each

marks.s2a: the Hundred that remains breaks into ten Tens
marks.s2b: the ten Tens join the two Tens to make twelve Tens
marks.s2c: three Tens go to each group

narration: <bookmark mark='s2a'/>Step two, regroup the Hundred that remains into ten Tens.
<bookmark mark='s2b'/>Ten Tens and two Tens make twelve Tens.
<bookmark mark='s2c'/>Twelve Tens divided by four gives each group three Tens.

marks.s3b: one One goes to each group

narration: <bookmark mark='s3a'/>Step three, share the Ones. We have four Ones to share into four groups.
<bookmark mark='s3b'/>Four Ones divided by four gives each group one One.

marks.s4a: the shares of one group are lined up
marks.s4b: the sum of one group is left blank

narration: <bookmark mark='s4a'/>Step four, put the shares of one group together.
<bookmark mark='s4b'/>Each group has three Hundreds, three Tens and one One.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>One thousand three hundred and twenty four divided by four is three hundred and thirty one.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the blocks
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's bubble shows 324 ÷ 4 = 81 with the Thousand block pushed aside; a check 81 × 4 = 324 falls one Thousand short; the bubble is crossed out

marks.doubt: the bubble with 81 appears and the Thousand block is pushed aside
marks.right: the Thousand breaks into ten Hundreds and joins the rest

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks one Thousand cannot be shared, so it is left out, and each group gets eighty one.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>But four groups of eighty one make only three hundred and twenty four. That is one Thousand short.
<bookmark mark='right'/>A block that cannot be shared is regrouped, never dropped. Regroup the Thousand into ten Hundreds and share them.
